balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals Limited): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals Limited): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals Limited): read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals Limited): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals Limited): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals Limited): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals Limited): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals Limited): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

grade.title: Ore grade (Li2O %)
grade.content:
Li2O grade is the lithia (lithium oxide) content of the spodumene concentrate PLS ships, the main driver of processing cost per tonne of contained lithium alongside unit cost.

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals): grade decline as the higher-grade zones of the Pilgangoora ore body are mined out is a named risk -- a lower grade means more ore must be processed (and more waste moved) for the same tonnes of spodumene concentrate, pushing unit cost FOB higher even if mining rates hold.

What to watch:

  • Sustained multi-year grade decline versus a single low quarter (blending/sequencing)
  • Grade trend against the unit cost FOB trend -- they should move together

operatingCosts.title: Total operating costs (FOB & CIF)
operatingCosts.content:
Operating costs FOB is the total mine-gate cost of producing and loading spodumene concentrate; operating costs CIF adds shipping and freight to deliver it to the customer's port (mostly China). Both are absolute dollar totals, not per-tonne.

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals): because PLS is a price taker on spodumene (it does not set the market price), the level and trend of these cost lines -- not revenue growth -- is what management actually controls and what determines survival through a price trough.

What to watch:

  • Costs falling in absolute terms during a downturn (deliberate curtailment/cost-out) versus rising (loss of cost discipline)
  • The CIF-FOB gap (freight) for shipping-rate exposure

unitCost.title: Unit cost (FOB & CIF) vs realised price per DMT
unitCost.content:
Unit cost FOB is the mine-gate cash cost per dry metric tonne (dmt) of spodumene concentrate shipped; unit cost CIF adds freight to land it at the customer's port. Realised price is what PLS actually received per dmt in the period.

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals): this is the single chart that decides the investment case. Spodumene is a commodity PLS cannot price -- the lithium cycle sets realised price, and PLS's only lever is where its unit cost sits on the global cost curve. Low-cost producers stay cash-generative and gain share when high-cost peers curtail production in a trough; PLS's own low-cost positioning (P680/P1000 expansions) is the thesis for surviving the current lithium downturn.

What to watch:

  • Realised price falling below unit cost FOB -- cash-negative before shipping is even paid
  • Unit cost FOB trending up as grade declines (see the grade chart) versus down from cost-out programs
  • The gap between FOB and CIF (freight cost, largely outside PLS's control)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals Limited): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For PLS Group Limited (formerly Pilbara Minerals Limited): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
